models.name: Baseline Random Forest (class_weight=None)
models.description: Standard unweighted Random Forest. Achieves high nominal accuracy (98.3%) with zero false alarms, but suffers from low minority recall (only 24.6% caught: misses 43 of 57 minority events) because unweighted Gini impurity prioritizes majority partition purity.
models.codeSnippet:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

# 1. Baseline model without class weights
rf_baseline = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=200,
    max_depth=12,
    class_weight=None,
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1
)
rf_baseline.fit(X_train, y_train)

models.name: Random Forest (class_weight='balanced')
models.description: Scales Gini impurity split criteria inversely proportional to global training class frequencies w_c = N / (K * N_c). Adds zero memory footprint and requires no resampling.
models.codeSnippet:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

# 2. Global inverse class frequency weighting: w_c = N / (K * N_c)
rf_balanced = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=200,
    max_depth=12,
    class_weight="balanced",
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1
)
rf_balanced.fit(X_train, y_train)

models.name: Random Forest (class_weight='balanced_subsample')
models.description: Computes class weights dynamically inside each bootstrap sample, automatically compensating for localized minority sampling variations across trees.
models.codeSnippet:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

# 3. Dynamic per-tree bootstrap subsample re-weighting
rf_subsample = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=200,
    max_depth=12,
    class_weight="balanced_subsample",
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1
)
rf_subsample.fit(X_train, y_train)

models.name: Random Oversampling (ROS) + Random Forest
models.description: Duplicates existing minority observations with replacement until classes are equal. Improves minority sample presence, but identical duplicate rows risk causing decision trees to overfit narrow noise points.
models.codeSnippet:
from imblearn.over_sampling import RandomOverSampler
from imblearn.pipeline import Pipeline as ImbPipeline
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

# 4. Pipeline with Random Oversampling
pipeline_ros = ImbPipeline([
    ('oversampler', RandomOverSampler(random_state=42)),
    ('classifier', RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, max_depth=12, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1))
])
pipeline_ros.fit(X_train, y_train)

models.name: Random Undersampling (RUS) + Random Forest
models.description: Randomly discards majority-class observations to match minority count. Ultra-fast training and achieves high recall (73.7%, catching 42 of 57 minority events), but suffers from significant information loss (discards 7,160 majority samples), generating 432 false alarms.
models.codeSnippet:
from imblearn.under_sampling import RandomUnderSampler
from imblearn.pipeline import Pipeline as ImbPipeline
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

# 5. Pipeline with Random Undersampling
pipeline_rus = ImbPipeline([
    ('undersampler', RandomUnderSampler(random_state=42)),
    ('classifier', RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, max_depth=12, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1))
])
pipeline_rus.fit(X_train, y_train)

models.name: SMOTE + Random Forest
models.description: Synthesizes new minority points along nearest-neighbor line segments. Avoids exact duplication, creating continuous generalization boundaries across minority space. Achieves the highest F1 score (0.472) and highest ROC-AUC (0.860) among resamplers.
models.codeSnippet:
from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE
from imblearn.pipeline import Pipeline as ImbPipeline
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

# 6. Pipeline with SMOTE nearest-neighbor interpolation
pipeline_smote = ImbPipeline([
    ('smote', SMOTE(k_neighbors=5, random_state=42)),
    ('classifier', RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, max_depth=12, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1))
])
pipeline_smote.fit(X_train, y_train)

models.name: Balanced Random Forest (imblearn)
models.description: Draws a bootstrap sample of the minority class and an equal-sized random subsample of the majority class independently for every individual tree in the forest. Eliminates global information loss because the full majority dataset is distributed across the forest.
models.codeSnippet:
from imblearn.ensemble import BalancedRandomForestClassifier

# 7. Balanced Random Forest: Independent per-tree downsampling
brf = BalancedRandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=200,
    max_depth=12,
    sampling_strategy="auto",
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1
)
brf.fit(X_train, y_train)
